frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a submitted nuclear cooperation agreement that is not successfully vetoed or overridden?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements transmitted by the President to Congress where a statutory review period applied and a joint resolution of disapproval was introduced and voted upon; excludes informal consultations and agreements under other legal authorities.
provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 3 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 major contested submissions examined in detail; zero historical instances of successful legislative blockage via joint resolution under the AEA framework.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments and peaceful nuclear cooperation extensions with smaller nations that did not reach floor votes for disapproval.
skeleton: Total 123 agreements submitted for congressional review since 1954 divided by successful blocks via joint resolution of disapproval
multiplier: 0 successful joint resolutions of disapproval enacted into law blocking a 123 agreement out of approximately 30+ major submissions
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks for 123 agreement congressional reviews remain stable under the Atomic Energy Act unless major legislative reform occurs.
